summary.name: Keka
summary.one_liner: Keka is a macOS file archiver for compressing, extracting, and encrypting archives, with drag-and-drop from the Dock.
use_cases: compress files or folders on a Mac
password-protect and encrypt files before sharing
split large files to fit email or server limits
extract archives of many formats on macOS
set up drag-and-drop compression from the Dock
summary.what_it_does: Keka compresses files and folders into archives by dragging them onto its Dock icon or window, without needing to open the app. It creates encrypted archives, using AES-256 for 7z files and Zip 2.0 legacy encryption for Zip files. It can split large archives into pieces that rejoin on extraction. The page lists a broad set of formats it handles, including 7Z, ZIP, TAR, GZIP, BZIP2, XZ, DMG, ISO, and many others, with extraction support for additional formats such as RAR and MSI.
notable: Drag and drop onto the Dock icon to compress without opening the app
Older macOS versions downloadable (back to Mac OS X 10.4)
Listed as open source in the awesome-mac directory
caveats: Buying from the Mac App Store supports development; the website version is free to download, and a tip is optional
Zip files use legacy Zip 2.0 encryption, which is weaker than AES-256
No beta is available at the moment
Setting Keka as default app requires a separate KekaExternalHelper download
